header.userPrompt:
Implement GitHub issue #79 in AlexITC/expense-tracker: warn on semantic duplicate bank statements at draft confirm time (account date-range overlap, implausible period length, period sanity), surfaced at confirm and as a badge on the statements list, warn-not-block. Full spec follows.

## Problem

The same bank statement can be imported twice as two separate statements, producing duplicate expenses that nothing detects.

Observed case: the same monthly statement for one account was imported twice under two different filenames. Both covered the identical period and had the identical set of rows, yet they imported as two distinct statements linked to two distinct documents with two distinct sha256 hashes.

Why it slipped through: dedup today is byte-level only (sha256 of the file), enforced in `CreateBankStatementDraftAction` and by the `document_user_sha256_unique` and `bank_statement_document_id_uq` constraints. A re-exported or re-downloaded PDF of the same statement has different bytes, so a different sha256, so none of those fire. The duplicate is semantic, not byte-identical.

The resulting duplicate expenses are also invisible to the existing expense dedup UI, because both sides are row-linked (the detector only pairs a row-linked expense with a non-row one).

## Goal

Add a semantic duplicate guard for bank statements. Warn the user, never hard-block. Getting explicit confirmation to proceed is the bar.

## Phase 1 (this issue)

At draft confirm time (`ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction`, where a ready draft becomes a statement and the extracted metadata already exists), run these checks and, if any trip, return a warning the UI shows in a confirm dialog that the user can explicitly accept:

1. **Date-range overlap on the same account.** Compare the incoming `[period_start, period_end]` against existing statements for the same account, scoped by `(bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency)` (there is no account entity). Warn on any range overlap, not just an equal period, so re-imports whose extracted dates drifted still trip it.
2. **Implausible period length.** Warn when `period_end - period_start` is not roughly one month (about 26 to 35 days). Covers a clean calendar month and a cycle like the 3rd to the 2nd.
3. **Period sanity (cheap, same warn path).** Warn when `period_start > period_end`, or when `period_end` is in the future.

Rules are warnings only. Nothing blocks the import; the user confirms and proceeds.

**Also surface the overlap check (rule 1) as a badge on the statements list page**, so pre-existing duplicates (like the case above) are visible without re-importing. Same query, second entry point.

## Out of scope (possible follow-ups)

- **Row-fingerprint match**: warn when the incoming row set (date + amount + description) substantially matches an existing statement's, even when the extracted periods differ. This is the strongest semantic signal and the true "dedup per content", but needs the parsed rows and a similarity threshold. Add only if period overlap proves insufficient.
- Gap / missing-month detection. That is a completeness feature, not dedup.
- A frontend sha256 pre-check. It compares bytes, so it would pass this case exactly like the backend did. Not worth building.

## Notes for the fix

- All user-owned queries must be scoped by `user_id`.
- Do not add a DB UNIQUE constraint on the metadata columns: they come from AI extraction and vary slightly between runs, so a hard constraint would be fragile. Keep it a confirm-time warning.
- Cleanup of an existing duplicate statement is separate: deleting the duplicate statement leaves its expenses row-less. Note those orphans have no receipt, so the current expense dedup UI does not surface them (see the dedup-flow improvement issue); that gap is tracked separately.

resultJson.description:
The same bank statement can be imported twice when the PDF bytes differ, for example after a re-download or re-export. Today's only dedup is the sha256 of the file, so the copy becomes a second statement and its expenses are duplicated. This epic adds a semantic duplicate guard that warns but never blocks. When a ready draft is confirmed (`ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction`), the backend checks the extracted metadata against three rules: (1) its [period_start, period_end] range overlaps an existing statement for the same account, keyed by (bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency) and scoped by user_id; (2) the period length (period_end − period_start in days) falls outside 26..35; (3) period_start > period_end, or period_end is in the future.

If any rule trips and the client has not accepted the warnings, confirm creates nothing and returns the warnings. The review page shows them in a dialog. "Import anyway" re-sends confirm with `acceptWarnings = true`, and the statement is created as usual. The overlap rule also appears on the statements list page as a "possible duplicate" badge, so existing duplicates are visible without re-importing.

No DB UNIQUE constraint is added, because the metadata comes from AI extraction and varies between runs. Rows are not fingerprinted, gap detection is not added, and cleaning up existing duplicates is not covered. All of these are out of scope.

tasks.title: Add user-scoped overlap queries to BankStatementDAO / BankStatementRepository
tasks.description:
Add two read queries that share one overlap predicate. Ranges are inclusive on both ends: `a.period_start <= b.period_end AND b.period_start <= a.period_end`. Rows must match exactly on bank_name, product_type, account_last4 and currency, and every table access needs `user_id = ?`.

(a) `BankStatementDAO.findOverlapping(userId: UUID, metadata: BankStatement.Metadata)(implicit conn): List[BankStatement]` returns the user's existing statements for that account whose period overlaps metadata.periodStart..periodEnd. Use the existing `parser` and `metadataColumns`, and order by period_start.

(b) `BankStatementDAO.overlappingStatementIds(userId: UUID)(implicit conn): Map[UUID, List[UUID]]` is a self-join of bank_statement, with both sides filtered by user_id and `a.id <> b.id`. It maps each statement id to the ids of the other statements it overlaps. Statements with no overlap are left out.

Expose both through `BankStatementRepository` as `Future`s in `database.withConnection`, following the style of the existing methods.

Tests go in `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepositorySpec.scala`, seeding through `RepositoryUtils.createStatement` / `createDocument` with custom `BankStatement.Metadata` and no raw SQL. Cover:
- an identical period matches
- a partial overlap matches
- a range that only touches on a boundary day matches
- adjacent non-overlapping ranges (Jan 1–31 vs Feb 1–28) don't match
- a different account_last4, currency, product_type or bank_name doesn't match
- another user's statement never matches
- `overlappingStatementIds` is symmetric and excludes self

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementRepositorySpec"`.

tasks.title: Show a 'possible duplicate' badge on the statements list
tasks.description:
Add `overlappingStatementIds: List[UUID]` to `GetBankStatements.Response.BankStatement` in `lib/api/shared/.../bankstatements/GetBankStatements.scala`. In `GetBankStatementsAction`, call `bankStatementRepository.overlappingStatementIds(userId)` alongside `all(userId)` and fill the field (`getOrElse(id, Nil)`).

Frontend, in `web/.../bankstatements/BankStatementsPage.scala` (`BankStatementList`):
- `toListStmt(updated)` builds the list model from a single `GetBankStatement.Response`, which has no overlap info. The polling merge must keep the previous value, e.g. `toListStmt(updated).copy(overlappingStatementIds = s.overlappingStatementIds)`, or `toListStmt` takes it as a parameter.
- Render a warning-coloured badge on the card (next to the filename or under the metadata line, using `var(--lc-warning-text)` as `gapWarning` does) when the list is non-empty.
- Put the badge text in a pure function in `BankStatementsLogic`, e.g. `duplicateBadgeText(s, all: List[BankStatement]): Option[String]`. Example: "⚠ Possible duplicate — overlaps <filename(s)>", resolving ids against the full list and falling back to a count if an id is missing.

Update every place that constructs the model so it compiles: `BankStatementsPage.toListStmt`, `web/src/test/.../BankStatementListSpec.scala` and `BankStatementsLogicSpec.scala` fixtures.

Tests:
- `BankStatementsLogicSpec` unit tests for the badge function: None when empty, names the overlapping files.
- In `server/src/test/scala/controllers/BankStatementsControllerSpec.scala`, the GET /bank-statements case where two statements share the same account and period lists each other. A statement for another account, or another user's, does not. Note that `PlayPostgresSpec.createBankStatement` always uses the same metadata, so two calls for one user already overlap. Seed distinct metadata where a non-overlap is needed, extending the helper with an optional metadata parameter if necessary.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementsControllerSpec"`, `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementsLogicSpec *BankStatementListSpec"` (web tests need Node 24 on PATH) and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Add the confirm-warning model and pure period/overlap checks
tasks.description:
Shared model, new file `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/bankstatements/ConfirmWarning.scala`:
- `ConfirmWarningKind` is a sealed abstract class with `entryName`, written in the same style as `AiSuggestionsStatus.scala`: a hand-written play-json `Format` that rejects unknown strings, plus `Schema.string`. Values: `Overlap`, `PeriodLength`, `PeriodOrder`, `FuturePeriod`.
- `case class ConfirmWarning(kind: ConfirmWarningKind, message: String)` with `Json.format` and a named `Schema`, e.g. `Schema.SName("BankStatementConfirmWarning")`.

Server: a pure object `net.wiringbits.actions.bankstatements.BankStatementConfirmChecks`.
- `periodWarnings(start: LocalDate, end: LocalDate, today: LocalDate): List[ConfirmWarning]`:
  - start > end gives PeriodOrder, and the length check is skipped in that case.
  - Otherwise, days = `ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(start, end)` outside 26..35 inclusive gives PeriodLength. Jan 1→Jan 31 = 30, Feb 1→Feb 28 = 27, and a 3rd→2nd cycle all pass.
  - end.isAfter(today) gives FuturePeriod.
- `overlapWarning(overlapping: List[BankStatement]): Option[ConfirmWarning]` returns a single Overlap warning whose message lists each overlapping period ("start → end"), or None when the list is empty.
- Messages are short, user-facing sentences that state the problem and the dates.

Tests: `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/BankStatementConfirmChecksSpec.scala`, a plain AnyWordSpec with no DB. Cover each rule, the boundary values 26 and 35 (no warning) and 25 and 36 (warning), the reversed period not also producing a length warning, end == today giving no future warning, and an empty overlap list giving None. Optionally add a JSON round-trip for `ConfirmWarningKind` next to `lib/api/shared/src/test/.../AiSuggestionsSpec.scala`.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementConfirmChecksSpec"`.

tasks.title: Return warnings from draft confirm and add an accept-to-proceed dialog on the review page
tasks.description:
API contract, in `BankStatementDraft.scala` inside `object Confirm`:
- Add `case class Request(acceptWarnings: Boolean)`.
- Change `Response` to `Response(bankStatementId: Option[UUID], warnings: List[ConfirmWarning])`.
- Give each its own format and schema name, e.g. "ConfirmBankStatementDraftRequest".
- Semantics:
  - Warnings non-empty and `acceptWarnings == false`: create nothing, leave the draft as is, and return `bankStatementId = None` with the warnings.
  - Otherwise: create the statement exactly as today and return `Some(id)`, echoing the warnings (empty if none).

Wiring:
- `BankStatementsEndpoints.confirmDraft`: add `.in(jsonBody[BankStatementDraft.Confirm.Request])` and change the input type to `(UUID, Confirm.Request, Future[UUID])`.
- `ApiClient.confirmBankStatementDraft(draftId: UUID, acceptWarnings: Boolean)`.
- `BankStatementsController.confirmDraft` takes the request.
- `ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction.apply(draftId, userId, acceptWarnings)`:
  - After `requireReconciled` / `requireMetadata` (hard errors stay hard errors), call `bankStatementRepository.findOverlapping(userId, metadata)`.
  - Build `warnings = BankStatementConfirmChecks.periodWarnings(ps, pe, LocalDate.now(clock)) ++ overlapWarning(...)`.
  - Short-circuit with `Future.successful(Response(None, warnings))` before any write when it must not proceed.
  - Log the warnings when proceeding.

Frontend, in `web/.../bankstatements/BankStatementTemplatePage.scala` (`BankStatementTemplateEditor`):
- `doConfirm` saves the draft, then calls `confirm(id, acceptWarnings = false)`.
  - `Some(stmtId)`: navigate to `/bank-statements/$stmtId` as today.
  - `None`: store the warnings in state (`Hooks.useState[List[ConfirmWarning]]`), set saveState back to Idle and open an MUI `Dialog` (title such as "This statement may be a duplicate").
- The dialog lists each warning message (`DialogContentText` with `withKey`) and has two actions:
  - Cancel: closes the dialog, nothing is created.
  - "Import anyway": calls `confirm(id, acceptWarnings = true)` and then navigates, or shows the error.
- Disable the buttons while busy.
- Build elements with `def` or inline, not object-level `val`s, and use the same Dialog style as the delete dialog in `BankStatementsPage.scala`.

Tests in `server/src/test/scala/controllers/BankStatementDraftControllerSpec.scala`:
- Update existing calls to `client.confirmBankStatementDraft(id, acceptWarnings = false)` and `.bankStatementId.value`. The default `reconcilingPayload` (Jan 1–31 2026, fresh user) trips no rule.
- New cases:
  - An overlapping statement for the same account (confirm one draft, seed a second draft with the same metadata) returns an Overlap warning with no statement id, and the draft is still listed.
  - Re-confirming with `acceptWarnings = true` creates the statement.
  - A different account_last4 gives no warning.
  - Another user's overlapping statement gives no warning.
  - A 60-day period gives PeriodLength.
  - Reversed dates give PeriodOrder. Check whether `requireReconciled` or other validation runs first.
  - A period ending in the future, relative to `LocalDate.now()` (the spec doesn't freeze Clock), gives FuturePeriod.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementDraftControllerSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`. If a frontend test exists for the template page, keep `BankStatementTemplatePageSpec` compiling and passing (`sbt "testOnly *BankStatementTemplatePageSpec"`).

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- lib/api/shared/: Tapir endpoints and request/response models, shared by server and Scala.js web. Endpoints: `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/endpoints/BankStatementsEndpoints.scala`. Client: `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/ApiClient.scala`. Around line 248: `def confirmBankStatementDraft(draftId: UUID) = handleRequest(BankStatementsEndpoints.confirmDraft, (draftId, dummyUserId))`; endpoints with a body pass a tuple like `(id, request, dummyUserId)`. Models: `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/bankstatements/`.
- server/: Play app. Layering is controller → action → repository → DAO (Anorm).
  - Controller: `server/src/main/scala/controllers/BankStatementsController.scala`. Each endpoint is a private method wrapped in `handleRequest { for { userId <- userIdF; r <- action(...) } yield Right(r) }` and registered via `BankStatementsEndpoints.x.serverLogic(x)` near line 255.
  - Actions: `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/`.
  - Repository: `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepository.scala`. Methods are `Future { database.withConnection { implicit conn => BankStatementDAO.x(...) } }` and run on DatabaseExecutionContext.
  - DAO: `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/BankStatementDAO.scala`. Anorm `SQL"""..."""` interpolation with `${id.toString}::UUID`, `#$metadataColumns` for the shared column list, `parser: RowParser[BankStatement]`, and `viewParser` for BankStatementView (which joins document for the filename plus row counts).
- web/: Scala.js + Slinky + MUI 5. Bank statement pages are in `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatements/`:
  - `BankStatementsPage.scala`: `BankStatementsPage`, plus `BankStatementList`, which renders cards, the delete Dialog, `gapWarning`, and `toListStmt`.
  - `BankStatementTemplatePage.scala`: the draft review/confirm page. `BankStatementTemplateEditor.doConfirm` currently does updateDraft, then confirmDraft, then `history.push(s"/bank-statements/${resp.bankStatementId}")`.
  - `BankStatementsLogic.scala`: pure helpers with unit tests in `web/src/test/.../BankStatementsLogicSpec.scala`.

KEY TYPES
- `BankStatementDraft` (shared) has `Metadata(bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4: Option[String], periodStart, periodEnd: Option[LocalDate], openingBalance, closingBalance)`, `Payload`, and `Confirm.Response(bankStatementId: UUID)`. Confirm currently takes no request body: `Endpoint[Unit, (UUID, Future[UUID]), ErrorResponse, Confirm.Response, Any]`, POST `bank-statements/drafts/:draftId/confirm`.
- `ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction`, deps `(bankStatementDraftRepository, bankStatementRepository, documentsRepository)(implicit ec, clock: java.time.Clock)`:
  - Loads the draft and parses the payload.
  - `requireReconciled` and `requireMetadata` throw RuntimeException; these stay hard errors. `requireMetadata` returns `BankStatement.Metadata(bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4, periodStart, periodEnd)` with trimmed strings.
  - Then `createConfirmedStatement(...)` and `draft delete`.
  - Use `LocalDate.now(clock)` for "today".
- `net.wiringbits.repositories.models.BankStatement`: id, documentId, userId, bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4, periodStart, periodEnd, createdAt, updatedAt. It also defines `BankStatement.Create` and `BankStatement.Metadata`. `BankStatementView` has the same fields plus documentFilename, totalRows, processedRows, extractionInfo, aiSuggestions, documentStatus.
- `GetBankStatements.Response(data: List[Response.BankStatement])`. Each item has id, documentFilename, documentStatus, bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4, periodStart, periodEnd, createdAt, totalRows, processedRows. It is built in `GetBankStatementsAction` and also in web `BankStatementList.toListStmt` (from `GetBankStatement.Response` while polling) and in web test fixtures (`BankStatementListSpec`, `BankStatementsLogicSpec`). Every construction site must be updated when a field is added.
- Shared enum convention (no enumeratum in shared models): see `AiSuggestionsStatus.scala`. It is a sealed abstract class with `entryName`, `values`, a hand-written play-json Format that rejects unknown strings, and `Schema.string`. Case classes use `Json.format` and `Schema.derived[...].name(Schema.SName("UniqueName"))`, and schema names must be globally unique.
- The account key has no account entity: (bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency). The web `BankStatementsLogic.accountKey` uses bank+product+last4 only, for grouping; that is fine and should not change.

CONVENTIONS
- Every user-owned query has `WHERE user_id = ?` on every table touched, including both sides of a self-join.
- Errors are raised by throwing RuntimeException in actions. handleRequest maps them to ErrorResponse, and clients see `.failed.futureValue.getMessage`. Warnings are not errors and must not be modelled as failures.
- No DB constraints or migrations for this feature.
- Tests:
  - Naming follows RULE-TE-001: the `should` subject is a method or behaviour, never the class name.
  - Repository specs extend PostgresSpec and seed via `server/src/test/scala/utils/RepositoryUtils.scala`, never raw SQL. Use `createStatement(stmt, metadata, rows)`, `createDocument(userId, sha256, kind = DocumentKind.BankStatementPdf)` and `sampleStatementMetadata`.
  - Controller specs extend `controllers.common.PlayPostgresSpec` with `withApiClient`. Each test creates a fresh user via `createVerifyLoginUser(tokenGenerator)`. Helpers: `createBankStatementWithRows` / `createBankStatement(userId)`, which always use metadata Test Bank/credit/USD/0000/2026-01-01..2026-01-31, so two calls for one user overlap.
  - `BankStatementDraftControllerSpec` has `reconcilingPayload` (BBVA/debit/EUR/1234, 2026-01-01..2026-01-31, a 30-day period that trips no rule) and `seedReadyDraft(userId, payload)`.
  - Actions are not unit-tested; pure helper objects are, with plain AnyWordSpec.
  - Frontend: prefer pure-function tests over DOM tests (RULE-TE-010).
- Frontend rules:
  - No object-level `val` holding a ReactElement or KeyAddingStage; use `def`.
  - Key every element in a list with `.withKey`.
  - Use `.build: ReactElement` when mapping MUI builders into lists.
  - Styles go through `new CSSPropertiesUtils { ... }` and CSS vars (`--lc-warning-text`, `--lc-error`, `--lc-brand`, `--lc-text-2`).
  - No setTimeout hacks.
  - `SaveState` (Idle/Saving/Failed) drives busy/error on the review page.
  - The dialog pattern to copy is `deleteDialog` in BankStatementsPage.scala: `mui.Dialog(true)(DialogTitle, DialogContent(DialogContentText...), DialogActions(Button...)).onClose((_, _) => ...).build`.
- Build and verify:
  - Targeted only: `sbt "testOnly *XSpec"`, plus `CI=true sbt Test/compile`, where `-Werror` is on and unused imports fail.
  - Do NOT run the full `sbt test`.
  - Run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before finishing.
  - Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default shell node v16 fails at yarn install).
  - `BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec` is known flaky under the full suite.
- Docs to respect: docs/guide/antipatterns.md, backend.md, frontend.md, testing.md.
